skill.name: blitz
skill.description: Coordinate parallel GitHub issue work using isolated git worktrees, structured agent delegation, review loops, and sequential merge steps.
skill.summary: Run multi-issue coding sprints with parallel agents and gated git worktree workflows.
skill.author: Cygnusfear

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown formatting, skill names, read-only inspection commands, or Mermaid examples. I confirmed the high-impact commands that can mutate GitHub or git state, and added one semantic finding for automated repository changes using authenticated credentials. No evidence of prompt injection was found.

remediation.issue: Authenticated repository changes can run without a clear approval gate.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before closing issues, creating or merging pull requests, posting reviews, force-pushing, or deleting branches.

remediation.issue: Command placeholders can be copied into shells with unsafe values.
remediation.suggestion: State that issue numbers, branch names, owner names, repository names, and worktree slugs must be validated before command execution.

remediation.issue: Parallel agents may act on stale or conflicting repository state.
remediation.suggestion: Add a human checkpoint after agent review and before each merge, rebase, force push, or cleanup step.

content.value_statement: Large issue backlogs are slow when fixes are handled one at a time. Blitz organizes parallel Claude agents in isolated git worktrees with review and merge gates.
actual_capabilities: Triages GitHub issues and identifies work that can run in parallel.
Plans one git worktree and branch for each independent issue.
Builds structured prompts for parallel Claude agent delegation.
Enforces full issue coverage through review and iteration loops.
Guides sequential squash merge, rebase, and cleanup steps.
Provides command and pitfalls references for GitHub CLI workflows.
limitations: Requires authenticated GitHub CLI, git worktree support, and Claude Code agent spawning.
Works best when issues are independent and have clear acceptance criteria.
Commands can modify branches, pull requests, and issues, so user approval is required.
Does not replace human review for risky, ambiguous, or conflicting changes.

use_cases.title: Clear a Maintainer Backlog
use_cases.description: Group independent issues, assign each to an isolated worktree, and review each pull request before merge.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Release Fixes
use_cases.description: Run several release blockers in parallel while keeping merge order and rebases controlled.

use_cases.title: Manage Personal Bug Sprints
use_cases.description: Turn multiple small bug reports into separate agent tasks with clear coverage checks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Blitz Sprint
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a small backlog.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Blitz to review these GitHub issues. Identify which issues are independent, which need deferral, and which approval checkpoints are required.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Agent Assignments
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate setup before parallel work begins.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Blitz to create a worktree and agent assignment plan for these issues. Include full requirements, branch names, and review criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Run Review Iterations
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced coordination while pull requests are active.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Blitz to inspect these pull request reviews. For each incomplete PR, write the follow-up prompt that restores full issue coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Control Merge And Cleanup
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced finalization after all reviews pass.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Blitz to choose a safe merge order for these ready pull requests. Include issue-link checks, rebase checkpoints, and cleanup approval steps.

output_examples.input: I have six independent bug issues and want a parallel sprint plan.
output_examples.output: Blitz groups fixable issues, proposes worktrees and branches, and prepares agent prompts with each issue requirement.

output_examples.input: A pull request scored eight out of ten and missed one acceptance criterion.
output_examples.output: Blitz produces a focused follow-up prompt that names the missing requirement and requests a new review pass.

output_examples.input: Four pull requests are ready, but they may conflict during merge.
output_examples.output: Blitz recommends merge order, issue-link checks, rebase checkpoints, and cleanup steps after approval.

best_practices: Extract every requirement and acceptance criterion before assigning an agent.
Keep one worktree, branch, and pull request per independent issue.
Confirm coverage, tests, review quality, and user approval before every merge.
anti_patterns: Running Blitz on tightly coupled issues that edit the same files.
Allowing agents to merge, force-push, or delete branches without approval.
Skipping the final requirements table before merging a pull request.

faq.question: What does Blitz help automate?
faq.answer: It helps plan and coordinate parallel issue work using git worktrees, Claude agents, reviews, and sequential merges.

faq.question: Which tools are required?
faq.answer: It expects GitHub CLI authentication, git worktree support, and Claude Code with agent spawning available.

faq.question: Can Blitz work with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow concepts apply to Codex, but some steps reference Claude Code agent features.

faq.question: Is it safe to let agents merge automatically?
faq.answer: No. Use explicit human approval before merges, force pushes, issue closures, and cleanup commands.

faq.question: When should I avoid Blitz?
faq.answer: Avoid it when issues are unclear, highly coupled, security sensitive, or likely to conflict heavily.

faq.question: How does Blitz reduce merge conflicts?
faq.answer: It separates work by issue, uses isolated worktrees, and merges pull requests sequentially with rebase checks.
